title: 2020 roadmap on pore materials for energy and environmental applications
claim: Conductive MOF supercapacitor electrodes benefit from accessible ion-transport channels, while redox-active centers can add pseudocapacitive charge storage.
explanation: The review contrasts ion-accessible stacked Ni3(HITP)2 layers with a conductive Ni-HAB electrode containing redox-active hexaaminobenzene centers.
scope: Conductive MOFs used as supercapacitor electrodes.
conditions: Electrolyte ions must be able to enter the relevant pores.
caveats: The reported capacitances are material-specific examples and should not be generalized to all conductive MOFs.
